subject: environmental-science
title: Eutrophication and Aquatic Stress
welcome_lead: When nutrients overload, lakes turn green and dead zones spread.
meta_desc: A-Level Environmental Science adventure on water pollution, eutrophication, BOD and COD.
final_note: High BOD signals microbes breathing oxygen out of the water — and life out of the lake.

concepts.def: Nutrient enrichment of water (especially N, P) causing algal blooms and hypoxia.
Biochemical oxygen demand — O₂ consumed by microbes over 5 days at 20°C (mg L⁻¹).
Chemical oxygen demand — O₂ equivalent of chemical oxidation of pollutants.
Dissolved O₂ <2 mg L⁻¹, killing fish and benthic fauna.
Rapid proliferation of phytoplankton, often cyanobacteria producing toxins.
Hypoxic ocean area, e.g. Gulf of Mexico ~15 000 km² each summer.

walkthroughs.body_html: Excess N and P fuel algal blooms; bloom death feeds bacteria, raising BOD; O₂ collapses; fish die.
BOD reflects biodegradable load; COD includes recalcitrant chemicals. Clean rivers <3 mg L⁻¹ BOD; raw sewage ~300 mg L⁻¹.
EU designates Nitrate Vulnerable Zones (NVZs); farmers limit fertiliser timing and quantity.

mcqs.q: Which value of dissolved oxygen defines hypoxia?
options: <2 mg L⁻¹
<8 mg L⁻¹
<15 mg L⁻¹
<20 mg L⁻¹
O₂ consumed by microbes degrading organic matter
O₂ produced by photosynthesis
Salinity of the water
Temperature-dependent solubility

mcqs.q: How does fertiliser runoff cause aquatic dead zones?
options: Fertiliser directly poisons fish.
Bacteria produce them.
Excess nutrients fuel algal blooms; when algae die, decomposition depletes water oxygen.
Fertiliser makes the water too acidic.

mcqs.q: Why are top predators most affected by persistent pollutants like mercury?
options: Biomagnification concentrates pollutants at each trophic level up the food chain.
Predators have weaker immune systems.
Fertiliser makes the water too acidic.
Predators are exposed to more pollution directly.

mcqs.q: How are most microplastics formed in the environment?
options: They are all manufactured at microscopic size deliberately.
Fertiliser makes the water too acidic.
Larger plastic items break down physically into smaller fragments over time.
Bacteria produce them.
